title: Constellation Area Locator
description: An astronomical database tracks star coordinates on a two-bit plane grid. Design a system that supports adding star coordinates and querying the total number of axis-aligned squares that can be formed using a given query point as one of the corners and three existing stars from the database.
constraints: There will be at most 3000 calls in total to add and count.
At any point, duplicate stars can be added and should be treated as separate instances.
input_format: A stream of operations: initializing the tracker, adding points [x, y], and counting squares for a query point [x, y].
output_format: An integer representing the total number of valid squares formed.

examples.explanation: Adding stars at (3, 10), (11, 2), and (3, 2). Querying at (11, 10) finds that it forms a valid square with the other three points, returning 1.
No matching points exist yet, returns 0.
Adding a duplicate corner does not complete a new distinct axis-aligned square configuration without the other vertices.
